how: A member proposes a recognizable mark and location without treating later helpers as part of the starter role.
Repeated calls gather builders for the Brand, subsequent pictures and holding existing work.
A proposed mark supplies the object around which build calls gather.
Build calls are followed by placing reports and requests for a picture that would let helpers contribute.
A stated shortage of workers and an approaching freeze prompt renewed recruitment.
Scarce hands are explicitly answered with recruitment while the stated moving rationales are destruction, cooperative adjacency and preventive avoidance.
A helper accepts a build call with a bare yes.
A bare No followed by shut preserves a refusal without reasons alongside the observed bare acceptance.
A participant asks what the canvas is and receives an explanation of its shared graffiti surface.
A hostile reply is visible without evidence of withdrawal under strain or repair of the quarrel.
Builders select forms and revise their size and alignment to accommodate adjacent pieces.
Participants report starting and later correct apparent placements as failed registration.
Anchor pixels, coordinates, templates and shading corrections make construction actionable.
Template-guided moving remains incomplete and does not by itself demonstrate that thread disagreement was settled.
Organizers invite builders into chat and bring its relocation rationale back into the public thread.
Replacing an expired invitation restores access to the advertised planning venue.
A public repair task lets helpers contribute without joining the chat, so invitations cannot imply universal chat participation.
Opening a project chat among existing fandom builders does not establish a distinct canvas-born faction or a newly shared identity.
Public invitations and returned instructions show coordination but do not establish hidden plans or rival infiltration.
Instructions allocate defense to those not making the next picture and provide a separate task for helpers outside chat.
The aggregate prevalence claim cannot erase local task allocation or turn host posting sanctions into authority over canvas placements.
Apparent placement is identified as a registration bug and the builder restarts.
Failed registration and restarting do not establish machine placements or activity beyond the timer.
The bug correction provides no evidence of scripts, spare accounts or automated construction.
Upkeep strain is visible but no machine-hands response is observed, leaving the specified mechanism untestable here.
A five-minute defense pledge supplies intended cadence but not evidence of sleep loss, device limits or other personal-time costs.
A helper repairs the known old form until missing relocation notice is explained, fitting the revised account of repair.
Builders defend the existing Brand while others extend the display and repeatedly spend placements against vandals.
An already placed Brand becomes a defense task while other builders make the next picture.
Participants attribute red-bombing to outsiders and distinguish their own intentional teardown from unwanted damage.
Repeated destruction prompts abandoning the old Brand and discussing another location.
Builders rearrange existing pieces for cooperative adjacency and rebuild higher to avoid an approaching taskbar before completed loss.
A builder weighs the red background's lower filling requirement against existing interference and crowded alternative sites.
Moving includes telling helpers to stop repairing the abandoned version.
Preventive relocation includes publicly explaining intentional erasure and telling helpers not to restore the old target.
A helper's explanation of obsolete repair is answered by asking for greater visibility for the relocation notice.
A planned relocation returns from chat to the public thread as an explanation of apparently destructive work.
Neighbours propose a truce and report a space-sharing deal that keeps related pieces together.
An allied member offers help and is welcomed into the coordination chat.
Builders describe shared-window artwork and coordination across neighbouring communities.
The taskbar threat is answered with an explicit joint-window plan to route the bar beneath the shared art.
A participant invokes coordination and noninterference when asking others not to sabotage a neighbouring logo.
Invoking a coordinated arrangement supports a restraint appeal but does not establish compliance by every helper.
Upkeep and truce talk occur without an explicit account that erosion produced this negotiation.
The offered help cites the neighbour's good condition rather than explicitly linking delivered aid to the recipient's shortage.
Help offers and border requests do not show a settled border producing an exchange of delivered assistance.
Offering to approach a host establishes proposed envoy action but not completed representation or an answered request.
Expected permission for red art is hearsay and the proposed contact yields no visible host ruling.
Questioning abandonment, missing notice and opposing a logo do not explicitly dispute representation or state its limits.
A reported deal receives a logistical question rather than a visible disclaimer of authority or refusal of its binding force.
A complaint about encroachment does not supply an argument over the fairness of covering others' work.
Insisting that neighbouring fandom marks stay together does not establish any speaker's membership in both rooms.
A vandalism report is answered through familiar fandom lore while builders also call contested work a task for strugglers.
A single joke recasts reported canvas vandalism through a fictional antagonist without evidence of a running gag being adopted.
The fictional-antagonist joke does not identify a pre-existing quarrel with a real canvas opponent.
Lore attached to vandalism does not itself name a real inherited rival in an attack turn.
Reporting that an unspecified joke was poorly received does not reveal an argument over offensive words or hate symbols.
Believable fake hiatus, spoiler and season announcements are revealed or challenged as April Fools misdirections.
April Fools also licenses making and sharing non-canvas fan-work variants rather than only deceptive announcements or takeovers.
A wish for a subreddit takeover and a remembered refusal cannot be treated as an enacted takeover.
A surviving date announcement with a removed body does not reveal the conduct that body contained.
The host funnels canvas talk into one permitted topic or chat and threatens sanctions for additional topics.
The moderator explicitly gives an influx of canvas topics as the reason for restricting further posting.
The stated sanctions remove threads rather than threaten destruction of the room's own canvas mark.
Participants celebrate completion, thank builders and claim the artwork as a collective accomplishment.
Reported completed Brands become objects of public thanks and pride.
Completion celebration can be provisional and coexist with an explicit statement that work is not over.
Celebration is followed by invitations to a next project on the same canvas rather than only a terminal memorial stage.
A not-over reply and a defense instruction qualify celebration of the existing Brand.
An edited closing report records the result while explicitly preserving the unfinished Behelit move.
Celebration and a final-result report share an edited item without independent evidence that celebration prompted recording.
Starting another picture on the same canvas does not establish carrying the effort beyond this event.
A final report is visible but no record-led continuation beyond the canvas is supplied.
Post-close lore and placement complaints do not contest a kept canvas copy or a historical account.
An allied member enters through canvas work and is welcomed without evidence of subscriber growth or joining ordinary fandom activity.
A sighting and celebration show the work being noticed but not a bid for creators', companies' or press attention.
A neighbour reports encroachment by the room's artwork without establishing organized attack intention.
A complaint about running over another work supports reported damage but not a verified deliberate raid.
An unspecified joke report and local logo rebuke do not establish room-spoken rivalry even at the one-taunt scale.
Build calls and a later encroachment complaint do not show recruits being turned toward an attack.
A reasoned restraint plea is visible but not as a response to a visible attack call.
The reported deal is not presented as an answer to an attack call.
Damage complaints and isolated rebukes do not show an attack generating a verbal-rivalry sequence.
